expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".

summary: The candidate quickly diagnosed the correct root cause — the sweep releasing original rather than remaining unit counts — by reading the failing test and tracing the sweep code, then made a targeted fix that passed the suite. The session was efficient and well-narrated but ended abruptly after the green run without any spoken reflection tying the fix back to the mechanism.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate went straight from reading the failing test to tracing the sweep code without asking any clarifying questions, but the session was short and the test failure was self-explanatory enough that there was little genuine ambiguity to resolve. There is no evidence of a clarifying question being asked or needed beyond what the test already revealed.

Before editing, the candidate read the test, correctly diagnosed the exact symptom (expected five but got eight, meaning shipped units were phantom-restocked), and stated the specific mechanism they intended to fix — swapping original count for remaining count in the release path. This is a mechanism-level hypothesis, not just a location, and it matches the actual root cause.

The candidate narrated each step of their reasoning in real time: what the test file showed, what the diff between expected and actual values implied, and the exact code change they were about to make. This narration is enough that an interviewer could follow the full path from symptom to fix without needing to interrupt.
The edit to src/sweep.ts directly matches the stated plan of swapping the original count for the remaining count in the release computation, with no scattered or contradictory changes observed.

The candidate re-ran the full test suite after saving and confirmed a pass before ending the session, which is the minimum verification step; however, they did not narrate checking edge cases (e.g. full-release holds) beyond the one failing test going green.

The candidate ended the session immediately after the passing test run with no verbal wrap-up connecting the fix back to the root cause — no statement of why releasing the original count created phantom stock or why the remaining-count fix resolves it beyond the test passing. Given the opportunity right after the green run, this is a missed articulation of the mechanism.
